heading: LOGOS-MODULE-PACKAGE-MANAGER
text: LOGOS-MODULE-PACKAGE-MANAGER

heading: Abstract
text: Abstract

heading: Abstract
text: Every Package Manager provider MUST be a local module provider backed by a local module instance.

heading: Abstract
text: Runtime MUST maintain ordinary provider and lifecycle records for its module instance.

heading: Abstract
text: An implementation MAY co-locate or statically link Package Manager code.

heading: Abstract
text: Runtime MUST represent that code as a direct-mode local module instance.

heading: Abstract
text: Remote facades MUST NOT be bound as Package Manager providers in this revision.

heading: Abstract
text: Host or deployment services that are not module providers MUST NOT be bound as Package Manager providers in this revision.

heading: Scope
text: Scope

heading: 1. Responsibility Split
text: 1. Responsibility Split

heading: 1. Responsibility Split
text: Package Manager MUST NOT run package-provided installation scripts while inspecting, resolving, installing, updating, or removing a package.

heading: 1. Responsibility Split
text: It MUST materialize selected artifacts under Package Manager or deployment control before Runtime or Module Loader uses them.

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: 2. Logos Package Eligibility

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: It MUST also contain a compatible, complete artifact variant.

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: It MUST contain signature material accepted by the active package-signing profile.

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: LGX inputs MUST satisfy the LGX structure and validation rules defined by this specification.

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: Nix inputs MUST realize an output that satisfies the Nix profile defined in Section 7.3.

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: It MUST verify the package signature before reporting package material as installed or producing Runtime handoffs from that material.

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: Archive names, catalog metadata, Storage metadata, and producer-specific build metadata MUST NOT override the canonical manifest.

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: The manifest MAY be authored directly or generated during package production.

heading: 2. Logos Package Eligibility
text: It MUST NOT infer missing package facts from backend-specific metadata.

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding
text: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding
text: A conforming LGX package MUST contain the canonical manifest at:

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding
text: It MUST be validated against the normative CDDL defined in Section 4.

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding
text: An LGX package MAY also contain a diagnostic JSON rendering at:

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding
text: If present, it MUST represent the same decoded value as `manifest.cbor`.

heading: 3. Manifest Location And Encoding
text: When the canonical CBOR manifest is present, Package Manager MUST NOT use the JSON rendering as the source of package identity, schema identity, artifact identity, or permission declarations.

4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: The schema and default artifacts MUST exist in every package variant in which the module's implementation artifact exists.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: Different module declarations MAY reference the same schema or default artifact.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: Within one module declaration, implemented contract commitments, required contract commitments, and requested permission names MUST each be unique.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: The implementation artifact referenced by each module declaration MUST occur in at least one package variant and MUST have kind `module-binary` wherever it occurs.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: Package Manager MUST reject a manifest whose arrays violate these ordering or uniqueness rules.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: Package Manager MUST verify each referenced artifact against its signed manifest hash before parsing or validating its content.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: A missing artifact, incorrect artifact kind, or hash mismatch MUST fail with `artifact-integrity-failed`.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: Invalid CDDL, a document schema-commitment mismatch, an absent or invalid root, an unresolved non-common schema reference, or an invalid default value MUST fail with `invalid-package`.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: When a manifest value commitment is required, the value commitment MUST bind the decoded deterministic CBOR value to:

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: When a manifest value commitment is required, the value commitment MUST bind the decoded deterministic CBOR value to: … the semantic commitment-model revision identifier;

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: When a manifest value commitment is required, the value commitment MUST bind the decoded deterministic CBOR value to: … the schema root for `logos.package_manifest`;

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: When a manifest value commitment is required, the value commitment MUST bind the decoded deterministic CBOR value to: … the schema subtree root for `logos.package_manifest.manifest`;

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: When a manifest value commitment is required, the value commitment MUST bind the decoded deterministic CBOR value to: … the normalized Logos value model for the manifest value.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: The signed claim MUST bind the exact manifest value commitment, including its commitment-model revision, schema roots, value root, hash profile, and hash suite.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: Package Manager MUST still hash the selected materialized artifact bytes and compare them with the signed manifest before use.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: Package Manager MUST reject a package when the signature is missing, the signer is not accepted by active trust policy, the signature is invalid, or the signed commitment does not equal the commitment computed from `manifest.cbor`.

heading: 4. Manifest Schema Identity
text: Catalog entries, Storage metadata, Nix metadata, archive names, and diagnostic JSON MUST NOT override the signed manifest claim.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: That input MUST bind each accepted trust-anchor identifier to its public key or other profile-defined verification material.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: It MUST also bind each accepted signer to a non-empty set of exact package names for which that signer is authorized.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: It MUST NOT use case folding, Unicode normalization, prefixes, wildcard patterns, or an authorization covering every package name.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: Package Manager MUST verify each package against the currently accepted package-signing trust anchors and require the authenticated signer to be authorized for the exact package name in the signed manifest.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: If no accepted anchor validates the signer and signature, or if that signer is not authorized for the exact package name, Package Manager MUST reject the package with `signature-verification-failed`.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: Package Manager MAY cache successful signature verification.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: It MUST invalidate an affected cache entry when the corresponding signature profile, trust anchor, signer, or exact-name authorization is no longer accepted.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: One signer MAY be authorized for multiple exact package names, and multiple signers MAY be authorized for the same exact package name.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: Trust-anchor or signer rotation MAY accept old and new identities for that exact package name during a configured overlap period.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: After an anchor is removed or revoked, Package Manager MUST NOT use it for a new successful resolution, installation, update, or Runtime handoff.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: Catalog trust MAY authenticate catalog claims, but it MUST NOT replace verification of the package's own signature and artifact hashes.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: Package material, catalog metadata, Storage content, and Nix metadata MUST NOT add, replace, or reactivate a package-signing trust anchor.

heading: 4.1 Package-Signing Trust
text: A local development deployment MAY configure its own package-signing trust anchor through the same protected trust-input path.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: A selected package-signing or catalog profile MAY additionally require transparency-log inclusion, a consensus checkpoint, or equivalent external anchoring.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: The profile MUST identify the accepted external trust root and verification rules through protected trust input.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: An address, log name, catalog field, downloaded key, or package-supplied checkpoint MUST NOT establish that trust.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: Catalog and external-anchor evidence MUST remain bound to the exact package signature and manifest commitment to which it applies.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: When active package-signing trust input requires revocation, a minimum accepted version, or fresh external-anchor evidence, Package Manager MUST enforce that requirement before a successful resolution, installation, update, or Runtime handoff.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: The selected profile MUST define any version comparison, trusted checkpoint, maximum evidence age, and rollback-detection rule it requires.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: Package Manager MUST retain the trusted state needed to reject an older signer state, checkpoint, or package state after accepting a newer one under such a profile.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: After loss of that state, it MUST re-establish freshness from protected trust input or fail operations that require freshness.

heading: 4.2 Catalog, External Anchoring, And Freshness
text: Failure to obtain fresh optional catalog data does not invalidate immutable installed bytes by itself, but Package Manager MUST NOT produce a result or handoff whose active trust requirements it cannot verify.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: Every conforming Package Manager MUST implement `logos.package-signing.cose-sign1-ed25519`.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text:
logos.package_manager.package_signing_profile =
  "logos.package-signing.cose-sign1-ed25519"

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: logos.package_manager.package_signing_key_id = bstr .size (1..128)

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: `manifest.cose` MUST be one tagged `COSE_Sign1` object using CBOR tag 18.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: The protected header map MUST contain exactly:

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: `manifest.cose` MUST be one tagged `COSE_Sign1` object using CBOR tag 18. The protected header map MUST contain exactly: … `alg` with COSE label `1` and value `-19` for `Ed25519`;

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: `manifest.cose` MUST be one tagged `COSE_Sign1` object using CBOR tag 18. The protected header map MUST contain exactly: … `kid` with COSE label `4` and a `logos.package_manager.package_signing_key_id` value.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: The unprotected header map MUST be empty.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: The outer `COSE_Sign1` object and serialized protected header map MUST use the core deterministic encoding requirements of RFC 8949 Section 4.2.1.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: The payload MUST be present as a byte string containing the Logos deterministic-CBOR encoding of `logos.package_manager.package_signature_claim`.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: Protected package-signing trust input MUST map each accepted `kid` to exactly one 32-byte Ed25519 public key encoded according to RFC 8032.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: Two accepted trust anchors MUST NOT use the same `kid`.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: Package producers MUST generate the 32-byte Ed25519 private seed with a cryptographically secure random generator and MUST protect it against disclosure and unauthorized signing.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: Package Manager MUST reject an object with a malformed tag or structure, non-deterministic CBOR, a missing or detached payload, an unknown or duplicate `kid`, any header not permitted above, an algorithm other than `-19`, an invalid public-key or signature length, or a failed signature verification.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: It MUST then decode the signed claim, require the exact profile identifier, recompute `manifest_commitment` from `manifest.cbor`, and require every commitment field to match the signed value.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: Any failure produces `signature-verification-failed` and MUST occur before artifact material is accepted or a Runtime handoff is produced.

heading: 4.3 Baseline Package-Signature Profile
text: An implementation MUST NOT infer freshness from successful signature verification alone.

heading: 4.4 Artifact And Catalog Signature Boundaries
text: 4.4 Artifact And Catalog Signature Boundaries

heading: 4.4 Artifact And Catalog Signature Boundaries
text: A detached artifact signature MUST NOT substitute for any step in that chain.

heading: 4.4 Artifact And Catalog Signature Boundaries
text: Catalog metadata MUST NOT establish signer trust, artifact integrity, package freshness, installation authority, or execution authority.

heading: 4.4 Artifact And Catalog Signature Boundaries
text: A deployment that requires authenticated catalog ordering, freshness, or external anchoring must select a catalog profile satisfying Section 4.2.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: A Package Manager MAY implement this profile.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: For an LGX source accepted under this profile, `provenance_object` MUST be present.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Package Manager MUST retrieve the identified object from the Logos Storage provider named by `storage` and MUST use that detached object as the profile's provenance evidence.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: It MUST NOT use an attestation embedded in the LGX archive to satisfy this profile.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: An absent locator, an unavailable object, a retrieval failure, or an object that does not satisfy every profile requirement MUST cause rejection without baseline-only fallback.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: The provenance object for this profile MUST be a standard DSSE v1 JSON envelope [DSSE v1] whose `payloadType` is exactly `application/vnd.in-toto+json`.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Its decoded `payload` MUST be one UTF-8 JSON in-toto Statement [in-toto Attestation v1] whose `_type` is exactly `https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1`, whose `predicateType` is exactly `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`, and whose predicate conforms to SLSA Build Provenance v1 [SLSA v1.2].

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: The envelope and decoded Statement MUST each be valid UTF-8 JSON containing exactly one value, contain no duplicate object member names, and have no trailing data.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: The `payload` and every `sig` value MUST use a base64 form permitted by DSSE v1, the `signatures` array MUST be nonempty, and every decoded `sig` value MUST be nonempty.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Package Manager MUST apply the DSSE and in-toto rules for unrecognized fields.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Package Manager MUST verify each signature over the DSSE pre-authentication encoding of the exact `payloadType` and decoded `payload` bytes.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: It MUST parse and evaluate the same payload bytes whose signature it verified.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: It MUST NOT normalize, reserialize, translate, or substitute the payload before signature verification.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: A translated or re-encoded representation does not retain the DSSE authentication and MUST NOT satisfy this profile.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Protected provenance trust input MUST bind each accepted provenance signer identity to a nonempty set of exact builder identifiers.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Protected deployment policy MUST select every accepted provenance-signing profile.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Each provenance-signing profile MUST define its signature algorithms, authenticated signer-identity construction, certificate or key requirements, revocation processing, and any required transparency verification.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: The envelope, Statement, `keyid`, builder, package, source, catalog, or caller MUST NOT select or weaken a provenance-signing profile.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: DSSE `keyid` is an unauthenticated key-selection hint and MUST NOT establish signer identity or trust.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Package Manager MUST evaluate each signature independently.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: A prefix, wildcard, redirect, case folding, Unicode normalization, or URI normalization MUST NOT establish equality.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Failure to obtain an accepted signer-builder pair MUST cause package rejection without baseline-only fallback.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: For this profile, at least one entry in the Statement's `subject` array MUST identify the complete gzip-compressed LGX archive bytes obtained from the package source.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: That entry's `digest` map MUST contain a `sha256` entry equal to SHA-256 [RFC 6234] over those exact bytes.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Package Manager MUST determine this subject match only from that `sha256` entry.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Subject `name`, `uri`, and digest entries using other algorithms MUST NOT establish the match.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Additional conforming subject entries are permitted and MUST NOT prevent a match established by any entry's required `sha256` digest.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Package Manager MUST compute that digest before decompression, extraction, normalization, or any other transformation.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: A manifest commitment, decompressed-archive digest, artifact digest, or module-binary digest MUST NOT substitute for the exact LGX digest.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Provenance naming the digest of one LGX object MUST NOT authorize another LGX object.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Build provenance for this profile MUST bind the LGX subject to the package source.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Protected deployment policy MUST associate each exact package name with a nonempty set of accepted `buildType` definitions.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Each accepted `buildType` definition MUST bind one exact `buildType` identifier to the external parameter that supplies the package source.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: It MUST define a deterministic mapping from that parameter to exactly one `resolvedDependencies` resource descriptor.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: The provenance predicate's `buildDefinition.buildType` value MUST equal the identifier of one definition associated with the exact package name in the signed manifest.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Matching MUST use case-sensitive exact string equality.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: A prefix, wildcard, redirect, case folding, Unicode normalization, or URI normalization MUST NOT establish equality.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: The provenance object, Statement, package, manifest, catalog, source, and caller MUST NOT do so.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Package Manager MUST apply the associated definition's mapping.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: It MUST reject provenance when the mapping selects no descriptor or more than one descriptor.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Protected deployment policy MUST associate each exact package name with a nonempty set of accepted source repository identifiers and accepted immutable source-identity rules.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: The selected source descriptor's `uri` MUST equal one of those identifiers as an exact case-sensitive string.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: The selected source descriptor's `digest` MUST contain at least one entry that protected policy recognizes as either a complete immutable source revision identifier or a source-tree digest.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: For Git, a `gitCommit` value MUST be the complete Git object identifier; an abbreviated object name does not satisfy this profile.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: A mutable branch or tag name MAY be retained as diagnostic information but MUST NOT substitute for an accepted immutable source identity.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: An additional protected source-evidence profile MAY require a Git commit signature, a SLSA Source Verification Summary Attestation [SLSA Source v1.2], or other independently authenticated evidence.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Such a profile MUST bind the evidence to exactly the same source repository identifier and immutable source identity, verify it under trust rules distinct from build-provenance and package-signing trust, and fail closed when required evidence is absent or invalid.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Source evidence MUST NOT replace build provenance or the package signature.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: A manifest, package sidecar, catalog, Storage object, Nix metadata, provenance object, or caller MUST NOT select, disable, or weaken that profile.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: When no package-provenance profile is selected, Package Manager applies the mandatory package-signature and artifact-verification baseline and MUST NOT claim that package provenance was verified.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: When protected deployment policy selects a package-provenance profile, Package Manager MUST enforce every requirement of that profile before a successful inspection, resolution, installation, update, or Runtime handoff.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: An implementation that does not support the selected profile MUST reject the protected policy configuration before accepting package material under it.

heading: 4.5 Optional Package-Provenance Enforcement
text: Missing, malformed, untrusted, stale, revoked, or otherwise non-qualifying provenance evidence MUST NOT cause fallback to baseline-only acceptance while a package-provenance profile remains selected.

heading: 7. Realization Profiles
text: 7. Realization Profiles

heading: 7. Realization Profiles
text: A conforming Package Manager implementation MUST support at least one realization profile defined by this specification.

heading: 7. Realization Profiles
text: If a request selects a source kind whose profile is not implemented, the implementation MUST return `unsupported-source`.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: 7.1 LGX Profile

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: The LGX profile installs prebuilt package material and MUST NOT build source code or run package-provided installation scripts.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text:
package.lgx
├── manifest.cbor
├── manifest.cose
├── manifest.json          optional diagnostic rendering
└── variants/
    └── <variant-id>/
        └── <artifact files>

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: The `variants/` directory MUST contain exactly one directory for each manifest variant.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: It MUST NOT contain files directly.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Each variant directory name MUST equal the corresponding manifest `id`.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Variant ids MUST be lowercase ASCII strings containing only letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Each variant id MUST form one non-empty path segment.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Archive paths MUST be relative, UTF-8, and Unicode NFC-normalized.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: They MUST NOT contain an empty segment, a `.` or `..` segment, a backslash, or a NUL byte.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: The archive MUST NOT contain duplicate normalized paths, symbolic links, or hard links.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: It MUST NOT contain device nodes, FIFOs, or other special files.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Package Manager MUST reject a selected variant whose paths collide under the selected platform's path-comparison rules.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Before writing an extracted entry, Package Manager MUST verify that its resolved destination remains within the selected installation root.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: LGX writers MUST order entries lexicographically by normalized path bytes.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: USTAR user and group identifiers and modification times MUST be zero.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: User and group names MUST be empty.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Directory modes MUST be `0755`, and regular-file modes MUST be `0644`.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Gzip headers MUST omit the original filename, use modification time zero, and use operating-system byte `255`.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Package Manager MUST bound compressed input size, decompressed size, archive entry count, individual entry size, and extracted output size before processing untrusted LGX input.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Package Manager MUST reject an archive before installation when any limit is exceeded.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: A present platform field MUST match the corresponding value supplied by the selected platform profile.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: It MUST return `incompatible-platform` when no variant is compatible.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Every regular file in a variant directory MUST be declared by exactly one artifact record in that variant.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Every declared artifact path MUST identify one regular file.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Every artifact referenced by a selected module declaration MUST occur exactly once in the selected variant.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Package Manager MUST omit it from the installed package record and MUST NOT produce a Runtime handoff for it.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Package Manager MUST verify required artifact hashes before exposing or installing the package.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: It MUST extract selected artifacts into a Package Manager or deployment-controlled location before Runtime or Module Loader uses them.

heading: 7.1 LGX Profile
text: Runtime and Module Loader MUST NOT execute code directly from an LGX archive or remote Storage object.

heading: 7.2 Profile Equivalence
text: 7.2 Profile Equivalence

heading: 7.2 Profile Equivalence
text: An implementation conforming through either profile MUST satisfy the same manifest, validation, installed-record, and handoff requirements.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: 7.3 Nix Profile

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: Package Manager MUST resolve `attr` using the Nix flake output rules for the selected target system.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: When `attr` is absent, it MUST select the flake's default package output for that system.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: The selected flake output MUST represent exactly one Logos package.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: A flake MAY expose more than one package output, but Package Manager realizes one selected output for each package operation.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: Before installation, Package Manager MUST resolve the source to an immutable realized output.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: The installed package source MUST record `locked_ref` unless `flake_ref` already identifies an immutable realized output.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: Package Manager MAY obtain the exact immutable realized output without a pre-verification isolation boundary only when protected deployment input selects that exact output and obtaining it performs no package-controlled Nix work.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: When obtaining the output requires package-controlled Nix work, Package Manager MUST establish a deployment-defined pre-verification isolation boundary before any such work begins.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: The boundary MUST contain the evaluator, every induced builder or hook, and every Nix service or store operation influenced by the unaccepted material.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: Protected deployment input MUST define and enforce the boundary's filesystem, process, network, credential, IPC, CPU, memory, storage, and time access.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: The work MUST NOT read or modify package-signing or provenance trust input, Package Manager installed state, deployment credentials, Runtime, Capability Authority, or Module Loader control surfaces, or other protected host state.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: It MUST NOT modify state outside its isolated store and disposable working state.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: Package Manager MUST treat the realized output as untrusted candidate material.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: It MUST verify the package signature, manifest, selected variant, and artifact hashes before reporting successful inspection, resolution, installation, update, or Runtime handoff.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: If no protected pre-resolved output is available and the required isolation boundary cannot be established, Package Manager MUST return `package-unavailable` before starting package-controlled Nix work.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: It MUST NOT fall back to unconfined local or remote evaluation or building.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: The realized output MUST contain the canonical manifest at:

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: share/logos/package.cbor

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: It MUST contain the corresponding package-signature container at:

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: share/logos/package.cose

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: The decoded manifest MUST validate as `logos.package_manifest.manifest`.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: Flake attributes and Nix package metadata MUST NOT define a second Logos package manifest.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: They MUST NOT override the embedded manifest.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: Package Manager MUST select a compatible manifest variant and verify its declared artifacts.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: It MUST produce the same installed package and Runtime handoff records required by the LGX profile.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: They MUST NOT appear in ordinary Package Manager results.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: Package Manager MUST NOT install packages into the user's ordinary Nix profile.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: It MUST maintain the roots or equivalent reachability needed to keep installed artifacts available while their installed package records remain active.

heading: 7.3 Nix Profile
text: It MAY use an existing Nix installation or a deployment-provided compatible service.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: 8. Validation Rules

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: Package Manager MUST validate package material before exposing it as installable or installed.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the required canonical manifest is absent.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest:

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … is not Logos deterministic CBOR;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … does not validate against `logos.package_manifest.manifest`;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … declares a package name or version that conflicts with the selected package reference;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … declares a package version or dependency requirement version that is not a permitted `package_version`;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … declares duplicate variant ids;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … declares duplicate artifact ids within a variant;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … references a module implementation artifact that is absent from every manifest variant;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … references a schema or default artifact that is not present exactly once in every manifest variant containing the referencing module's implementation artifact;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … declares duplicate package dependency names;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … declares duplicate module identities;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … assigns one artifact to more than one module declaration;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when the manifest: … contains an invalid schema commitment record.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: An LGX package MUST be rejected with `invalid-package` when its archive structure, entry types, paths, or encoding do not satisfy Section 7.1.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `incompatible-platform` when its platform or ABI constraints exclude the local host or selected runtime profile.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `package-unavailable` when the selected profile cannot materialize the selected package.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `artifact-integrity-failed` when:

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `artifact-integrity-failed` when: … a required artifact is missing from the selected variant or realized output;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `artifact-integrity-failed` when: … a manifest artifact path escapes its selected variant or realized output;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `artifact-integrity-failed` when: … an artifact omits its required hash;

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `artifact-integrity-failed` when: … an artifact hash does not match the materialized artifact.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: A package MUST be rejected with `signature-verification-failed` when its required signature is missing, invalid, rooted in an unaccepted signer or trust anchor, or bound to a manifest commitment other than the commitment computed from its canonical manifest.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: Manifest artifact paths MUST be relative paths.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: They MUST NOT be absolute paths.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: They MUST NOT contain parent-directory traversal.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: They MUST NOT identify remote resources.

heading: 8. Validation Rules
text: Diagnostic JSON renderings MUST NOT be used to override the canonical CBOR manifest.

heading: 9. Module Declarations

heading: 9. Module Declarations

heading: 9. Module Declarations
text: The `implements`, `requires`, and `requested_permissions` arrays MUST be non-empty when present.

heading: 9. Module Declarations

heading: 9. Module Declarations

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: The `dependencies` array MUST be non-empty when present.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Dependency package names MUST be unique within one manifest.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: A `compatible` requirement MUST NOT contain a pre-release version.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Protected deployment policy MUST supply a resolver-limit set containing positive integer limits for:

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Protected deployment policy MUST supply a resolver-limit set containing positive integer limits for: … distinct package names in one partial closure;

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Protected deployment policy MUST supply a resolver-limit set containing positive integer limits for: … dependency depth;

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Protected deployment policy MUST supply a resolver-limit set containing positive integer limits for: … candidate records considered for one package name; and

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Protected deployment policy MUST supply a resolver-limit set containing positive integer limits for: … candidate-assignment attempts in one root operation.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Package Manager MUST reject a protected policy configuration that omits a limit or supplies a non-positive value.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: A package, manifest, catalog, source, or caller MUST NOT select, raise, or disable a resolver limit.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Before adding a package name to a partial closure or inspecting a manifest at a greater depth, Package Manager MUST verify that the corresponding limit permits the operation.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Package Manager MUST consider candidates in the order defined below and MUST NOT consider another candidate for that package name after its limit is reached.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: The attempt counter spans the complete root operation and MUST NOT decrease during backtracking.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: If resolution would exceed any resolver limit before finding a complete closure, Package Manager MUST terminate the root operation with `dependency-unavailable`.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: It MUST NOT install a partial closure or modify installed package state.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Limit exhaustion and all counter values are determined by the installed state, catalog inputs, and protected policy and MUST NOT depend on implementation-local resource thresholds.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: To resolve, install, or update a root package, Package Manager MUST recursively inspect the selected dependency manifests and construct the transitive package closure.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: One closure MUST select at most one version of each package name.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Package Manager MUST detect a dependency cycle and fail the root operation with `dependency-unavailable`.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: A candidate MUST also satisfy the applicable manifest-commitment, realization-profile, platform-variant, signature, and artifact rules for the requested operation.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Its signature MUST validate under an accepted trust anchor, and its authenticated signer MUST be authorized for its exact package name.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Package Manager MUST exclude a candidate that fails this requirement before ordering candidate versions by SemVer precedence or exploring its dependency closure.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: An installed candidate with matching exact identity and manifest commitment MAY satisfy a dependency without being materialized again.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Resolution MUST be deterministic for the same installed state, catalog inputs, and protected policy.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: When a root package reference omits `version` and no source is supplied, Package Manager MUST select the highest available normal release under SemVer precedence.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: A pre-release root version MUST be selected by an explicit version or source.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: When a choice is required, Package Manager MUST select the unresolved package name that is first in UTF-8 byte order.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: It MUST consider that package's satisfying candidate versions in descending SemVer precedence.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: It MUST select the first candidate for which the complete transitive closure can be resolved, backtracking to lower candidates when a candidate's dependencies make the closure unsatisfiable.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: If multiple acceptable manifests claim the same package name and version with different manifest commitments, protected catalog policy MUST select one exact commitment, or the root operation MUST fail with `dependency-unavailable`.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: If no complete solution exists, the root operation MUST fail with `dependency-unavailable`.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: The `resolved_dependencies` array in an installed package record MUST contain one exact entry for every direct manifest dependency, in manifest declaration order.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: It MUST be empty when the manifest declares no dependencies.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Catalog changes MUST NOT alter the recorded dependency edges of an installed package.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Different installed closures MAY contain different versions of one package name, but one closure MUST NOT select more than one.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Package Manager MUST NOT infer a Logos package dependency from a module provider requirement, build metadata, or a realization backend's internal dependency closure.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: When no catalog source is available, an LGX operation can resolve a dependency only from a satisfying installed package; otherwise it MUST fail with `dependency-unavailable`.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: Package Manager MUST preserve requested permission declarations as module facts, but it MUST NOT convert them into runtime authority.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: `constraints` contains one Logos deterministic-CBOR value that MUST conform to the CDDL owned by that definition.

heading: 11. Dependencies And Requested Permissions
text: `reason` is explanatory package metadata and MUST NOT change the requested or granted scope.

logos.package_manager.runtime_handoff = {
  module: tstr .size (1..64),

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: A Runtime handoff MUST carry the selected installed module artifact and the exact manifest commitment accepted during package-signature verification.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: Its package identity and artifact id MUST equal the corresponding installed-record fields.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: Package Manager MUST derive the handoff artifact hash from the signed manifest and MUST NOT emit the handoff if the package is no longer accepted by active signing trust.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: When the signed module declaration contains `configuration`, the Runtime handoff MUST contain the corresponding configuration-owned `configuration_declaration`.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: The handoff MUST contain the schema document and default value rather than their package artifact identifiers, package paths, or installed paths.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: Package Manager MUST NOT emit the handoff unless the resolved declaration satisfies LOGOS-MODULE-CONFIGURATION and exactly matches the signed artifact references and declaration fields.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: Runtime MUST independently verify both roots in the configuration-schema commitment and every supplied value before use.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: Before a runtime host starts or exposes a module, active policy must decide whether the package and artifact may be used for the requested placement.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: The handoff MUST preserve the module declaration's `primary_contract`, `implements`, `requires`, and `requested_permissions` without adding or widening any declaration.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: Its `module` field MUST equal the module declaration's flat runtime module name.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: Runtime MUST validate selected providers against the relevant contract expectations before exposing ready invocation paths.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: For every local provider realized through Module Loader, Runtime MUST obtain the complete descriptor from the `call_surface` field of an active Module Loader realization record.

heading: 12. Runtime Handoff Records
text: It MUST require the descriptor's optional primary contract and implemented-interface set to match the handoff exactly.
